reference_title: Design of Mechanically Stabilized Earth Walls and Reinforced Soil Slopes, Volume II
chapter_title: Contracting Methods and Specifications for MSE Walls and Slopes

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: From its introduction in the early 1970s, the total construction value of MSE walls is estimated to exceed $2 billion. Hundreds of millions of dollars have been saved since the early 1980s by bidding alternates for retaining structures. Problems identified include misapplication of wall technology, poor specifications, lack of enforcement, inequitable bidding, poor construction, inadequate inspection, and inconsistent review and acceptance practices. MSE wall and RSS systems are contracted using two approaches: (1) Agency or material supplier designs with system components, drainage details, erosion measures, and construction execution explicitly specified; or (2) Performance or end-result approach using approved or generic systems with lines and grades noted on drawings and geometric and design criteria specified (followed by project-specific design review). Both contracting approaches are valid if properly implemented.
key_points: Two contracting approaches: Agency/supplier design vs. end-result/line-and-grade design
Each approach valid if properly implemented; choice depends on agency expertise and project criticality
Formal policy development recommended for uniformity within each Agency
sections.applicability: MSE walls and RSS contracting; policy development

sections.title: Policy Development
sections.body: Each Agency should develop a formal policy for MSE wall and RSS design and contracting. Policy objectives: obtain uniformity; establish standard policies and procedures for design review and acceptance; establish review/acceptance policy for new systems and components; delineate responsibility for plans preparation, design review, and construction control; delineate design responsibility for consultant and supplier plans; develop design and performance criteria standards; develop and update material and construction specifications; establish contracting procedures by weighing advantages/disadvantages of prescriptive vs. end-result methods.
key_points: Formal policy recommended to ensure uniformity across all Agency projects
Policy must address both Agency-prepared and supplier-prepared designs
Contracting method selection (prescriptive vs. end-result) should be documented policy decision
sections.applicability: Agency policy development for MSE/RSS programs

sections.title: System or Component Approvals
sections.body: Prior approval of systems or components is highly desirable. Supplier must submit: development history and year commercialized; organizational structure; limitations and disadvantages; prior users list; sample material and construction specifications; field construction manual; design calculations for typical applications; typical unit costs; independent performance evaluations. For geosynthetic approval, additional requirements: creep test results (ASTM D5262, 10,000-hr minimum); ultimate strength (ASTM D4595 geotextiles, ASTM D6637 geogrids at 10% strain rate); hydrolysis resistance (PET), oxidative resistance (PP, HDPE), stress cracking resistance (HDPE) for 75- and 100-year design life; installation damage reduction factors; joint strength (ASTM D4884, GRI:GG2); pullout interaction (ASTM D6706); direct sliding (ASTM D5321); QC program. HITEC program (ASCE) available for independent system review.
key_points: Prior approval required before including system in design phase or as value engineering alternate
Geosynthetic approval requires 10,000-hour minimum creep test per ASTM D5262
UV resistance per ASTM D4355 required for all products
HDPE: ASTM D1248 type/class/grade; PP: ASTM D4101 group/class/grade; PET: minimum IV (ASTM D4603) and maximum CEG (ASTM D2455)

tables.title: Minimum Conformance Tests for Geosynthetic Approval
tables.content: Wide Width Tensile: ASTM D4595 (geotextiles); Specific Gravity (HDPE): ASTM D1505; Melt Flow Index (PP/HDPE): ASTM D1238; Intrinsic Viscosity (PET): ASTM D4603; Carboxyl End Group (PET): ASTM D2455; Single Rib Tensile (geogrids): ASTM D6637

sections.title: Design and Performance Criteria
sections.body: Each Agency should formalize design and performance criteria in a design manual (Bridge Design Manual under Retaining Structures for MSE walls, Highway Design Manual for RSS). The design manual should adopt current AASHTO LRFD Bridge Design Specifications Section 11.10 (Mechanically Stabilized Earth Walls) as primary basis, with Agency-specific deviations and additions. Construction material specifications for MSE walls may be modeled on Section 7 of AASHTO LRFD Bridge Construction Specifications (2004). RSS performance criteria should be based on Chapter 9 data.
key_points: AASHTO LRFD (2007) Section 11.10 is primary design basis for MSE walls
AASHTO LRFD Bridge Construction Specifications (2004) Section 7 for material specs
Agency-specific deviations must be documented; RSS design based on Chapter 9 ASD approach

sections.title: Agency or Supplier Design
sections.body: This approach includes development of detailed MSE wall or RSS plans and material specifications in bidding documents. Advantage: complete design, details, and specs developed over longer design period; Agency engineers examine more options. Disadvantage: additional alternate design sets; newer systems may not be considered. Fully detailed plans must include plan and elevation sheets, facing/panel details, drainage facilities/special details, design computations, geotechnical report, and construction specifications.
key_points: Requires Agency staff trained in MSE/RSS technology
Plan sheets: plan view, elevations, reinforcement lengths/types, panel layout, drainage alignment
Design computations: internal/external stability and reinforcement life expectancy
Geotechnical report must establish bearing pressures, reinforced fill properties, and drainage
sections.applicability: Agency or supplier design contracting approach

sections.title: End Result Design Approach
sections.body: Also called 'line and grade' or 'two line drawing.' Agency prepares geometric requirements and material specifications; prequalified suppliers/components perform design. Benefits: trained and experienced supplier design staff; prequalified materials have track record of working together; lessens Agency engineering costs and transfers design cost to construction. Disadvantage: Agency engineers may not fully understand technology for approving construction modifications. Detailed designs submitted within 60 days of contract award for Agency review. Plans include: geometric requirements (plan, elevation, cross-section), geotechnical requirements, structural/design requirements (AASHTO references, external loads, drainage, erosion protection), and performance requirements (tolerable horizontal/vertical movement).
key_points: Bid quantities obtained from lines and grades; can be lump-sum or unit-price basis
Contractor/supplier responsible for internal and local external stability
Agency typically responsible for global stability, bearing, and settlement
Complete design drawings and calculations due within 60 days of contract award

sections.title: Standard Designs
sections.body: MSEW standard designs: Agency responsibilities include plan and front elevation views, drainage details, traffic barrier details. Standard design charts NOT applicable for: soft soils or high water; large quantity projects; slopes > 1:3 in front; wall height > 32 ft (7.0 m); tiered walls; walls with soundwalls. Contractor responsibilities include providing detailed drawings with reinforcement layout, wall facing layout, cross sections, elevation views, and PE certification. RSS standard designs: Agency responsibilities include review by Turf/Erosion Prevention and Environmental Services. Standard slope angles are 45 and 70 degrees. Not applicable for: soft soils with groundwater within depth H; large quantity projects; slopes above/below reinforced slope. Only Agency-approved products from the Approved Products List (APL) may be used.
key_points: MSEW standard designs max height: 32 ft (7.0 m); not for tiered walls or soundwalls
RSS standard slope angles: 45 degrees (Case 1A and 1B) and 70 degrees (Case 2)
Only APL-approved product combinations may be used in standard designs
PE certification required for both MSEW and RSS standard design submittals
sections.applicability: Standard design programs; Agency-maintained approved products lists

sections.title: Review and Approvals
sections.body: Checklist items requiring review: conformance to project line and grade; conformance of design calculations to Agency standards (design methods, allowable bearing, allowable tensile strength, connection design, pullout parameters, surcharge loads, factors of safety); development of design details at obstructions; facing details and architectural treatment. For end-result contracting: complete design drawings and calculations due within 60 days of contract award; review process similar to supplier design by Agency structural and geotechnical engineers.
key_points: Review must verify: line/grade conformance, calculation compliance, obstruction details, aesthetics
Both structural and geotechnical engineers must participate in review
End-result designs: 60-day submittal deadline after contract award

sections.title: Construction Specifications and Special Provisions
sections.body: Guide construction and material specifications are provided for: (1) Section 10.9 - Example specification for MSE walls with segmental precast concrete, WWM, or MBW facings and steel (grid or strip) or geosynthetic reinforcements; (2) Section 10.10 - Example specifications for RSS systems. Guide specifications should serve as technical basis for Agency standard specifications. Local experience and practice should be incorporated. Contractor required to submit quality control plan.
key_points: Unified specification for all MSE systems recommended regardless of contracting method
Material and construction requirements sufficiently well-developed for unified specifications
Contractor QC plan required to document measurements and documentation during construction

sections.title: Example Specification for Mechanically Stabilized Earth (MSE) Walls
sections.body:
Example specification modified from Arizona DOT (2009) LRFD MSE Wall specification. Applies to MSE walls with galvanized steel or geosynthetic reinforcement, with precast segmental panels, welded wire mesh (WWM), or masonry modular block wall (MBW) facings.

Section 1 (Description): General requirements, accepted pre-approved systems, manufacturer's field representative requirements (4 successful walls of similar height/complexity in past 3 years), pre-activity meeting requirements.

Section 2 (Submittals): Working drawings and design calculations must be sealed by registered Civil Engineer. Six complete sets; Agency has 30 calendar days for first review, 15 days for subsequent reviews. No wall construction until written NTP issued. Design must comply with FHWA NHI-10-024/10-025 and AASHTO (2007) 4th Edition. Simplified Method for maximum reinforcement loads.

Design Parameters (Table 1 of specification): Design life = 75 years; Retained fill phi >= 32 deg; Reinforced fill phi = 34 to 40 deg (max); Reinforcement length B >= 0.7H or 8 ft (whichever greater); Limiting eccentricity: B/4 soil, 3/8B rock (Strength), B/6 soil, B/4 rock (Service I); Resistance factors: sliding = 1.0; bearing = 0.65; deep-seated/compound stability = 0.65 (0.90 for earthquake); pullout static = 0.90, combined static/earthquake = 1.20; metallic strip static = 0.75, earthquake = 1.00; metallic grid static = 0.65, earthquake = 0.85; geosynthetic static = 0.90, earthquake = 1.20.

Section 3 (Material Requirements): Precast concrete min. 4,000 psi; tolerances: connection devices +/- 1 inch, panel squareness < 1/2 inch difference in diagonals. Galvanization: min. 2.0 oz/ft2 (605 g/m2) per AASHTO M111 (ASTM A123). Reinforcement strips: ASTM A572 Grade 65 min; Tie strips: ASTM A1011 Grade 50 min. MBW units: min. 4,000 psi compressive strength average (3,500 psi individual); min. 125 pcf dry unit weight; max 5% water absorption after 24 hrs; freeze-thaw testing per ASTM C1262 required. Modular block tolerances: length/width +/-1/8 inch, height +/-1/16 inch.

Backfill gradation (Table 2): 4-inch sieve = 100% passing; No. 40 sieve = 0-60%; No. 200 sieve = 0-15%; max particle size = 3/4 inch for geosynthetics. Plasticity Index (PI) <= 6 (AASHTO T90). Friction angle: min. 34 degrees (tested per AASHTO T236 on fraction finer than No. 10 sieve at 95% T-99). Electrochemical requirements for metallic reinforcement (Table 3): pH 5.0-10.0; resistivity >= 3,000 ohm-cm (chloride/sulfate waived if >= 5,000 ohm-cm); chlorides <= 100 ppm; sulfates <= 200 ppm. For geosynthetics (Table 4): polyolefin (PP/HDPE): pH > 3; polyester (PET): pH > 3 and < 9. Organic content < 1% all reinforcements.

Retained backfill: phi >= 32 deg (Agency value); percent finer No. 200 < 50%; LL < 40, PI < 20. Sampling frequency: reinforced fill = 1 per 2,000 CY for gradation/PI and electrochemical; 1 per material change for friction angle and Proctor. Retained fill = 1 per 5,000 CY for gradation/PI; 1 per material change for friction angle.

MBW spacing requirements: first layer no more than 16 inches above leveling pad; last layer no more than 20 inches below top; maximum spacing 32 inches. Metallic reinforcement for flexible face walls: max vertical and horizontal spacing 18 inches for permanent walls.

Section 4 (Construction): Foundation proof-rolling: 25-ton pneumatic-tired tandem-axle roller; rutting < 1/4 in acceptable; rutting 1/4 to 1-1/2 in: scarify and recompact; rutting > 1-1/2 in: remove and reconstruct; pumping > 1 in: remediate. Leveling pad: min. width = facing unit + 8 inches; top elevation within 1/8 inch of design; cure minimum 24 hours before facing placement. Compaction: 95% T-99 (or T-180) main zone; 90% T-99 within 3 ft of face; max lift 10 inches; moisture: w <= wopt within -3% (dry side). Wall tolerances (precast panels): horizontal/vertical alignment max 3/4 inch per 10-ft straightedge; plumbness max 1/2 inch per 10 ft; panel out-of-plane offset max 3/8 inch; joint gaps within 1/8 inch horizontal and 1/4 inch vertical of design. MBW tolerances: alignment 3/4 inch per 10-ft; plumbness 1-1/4 inch per 10 ft.

Section 5 (Measurement): Square foot of completed wall (top of wall to top of leveling pad). Section 6 (Payment): Unit price per square foot complete in place including design, materials, labor.
key_points: Design life = 75 years; reinforced fill phi >= 34 deg; L >= 0.7H or 8 ft min
Resistance factors: strip static 0.75/seismic 1.00; grid static 0.65/seismic 0.85; geosynthetic static 0.90/seismic 1.20; pullout static 0.90/seismic 1.20
Backfill: 4-in:100%; No.200:0-15%; PI<=6; phi>=34 deg; organic content <1%
Metallic fill: pH 5-10; resistivity >=3,000 ohm-cm; Cl<=100 ppm; SO4<=200 ppm
Geosynthetic fill: polyolefin pH>3; polyester pH>3 and <9
Compaction 95% T-99 main zone, 90% T-99 within 3 ft of face; moisture on dry side (w <= wopt)
Proof-rolling: rutting thresholds 1/4 in and 1-1/2 in; pumping > 1 in requires remediation
MBW: first layer <=16 in above leveling pad; max spacing 32 in; top layer <=20 in below coping

tables.title: MSE Wall Design Parameters
tables.content: Design life 75 yr; phi_retained >=32 deg; phi_reinforced 34-40 deg; B>=0.7H or 8 ft; phi_strip_static=0.75; phi_strip_seismic=1.00; phi_grid_static=0.65; phi_grid_seismic=0.85; phi_geosyn_static=0.90; phi_geosyn_seismic=1.20; phi_pullout_static=0.90; phi_pullout_seismic=1.20; phi_bearing=0.65; phi_sliding=1.0; phi_overall_stability=0.65

tables.title: Backfill Gradation Requirements
tables.content: 4-inch: 100% passing; No. 40: 0-60%; No. 200: 0-15%; max particle 3/4 in for geosynthetics

tables.title: Electrochemical Requirements - Metallic Reinforcements
tables.content: pH: 5.0-10.0 (AASHTO T-289); Resistivity min: 3,000 ohm-cm (AASHTO T-288); Chlorides max: 100 ppm (ASTM D4327); Sulfates max: 200 ppm (ASTM D4327); Note: if resistivity >=5,000 ohm-cm, chloride/sulfate requirements waived

tables.title: Electrochemical Requirements - Geosynthetic Reinforcements
tables.content: Polyolefin (PP/HDPE): pH > 3 (AASHTO T-289); Polyester (PET): pH > 3 and < 9 (AASHTO T-289)

sections.applicability: MSE walls with precast panels, WWM, or MBW facing; steel or geosynthetic reinforcement; LRFD design

sections.title: Construction Specifications for Reinforced Slope Systems
sections.body:
Four specification guidelines provided: (1) RSS Construction (Agency Design); (2) Erosion Control Mat or Blanket; (3) Geosynthetic Drainage Composite; (4) Proprietary Geosynthetic RSS Systems.

Agency should develop documented procedures for review and approval of: geosynthetic soil reinforcing materials; drainage composite materials; erosion control materials; geosynthetic reinforced slope systems and suppliers; in-house design and performance criteria for reinforced slopes.

RSS Geosynthetic Reinforcement (10.10.1): Geogrid or geotextile with sufficient mechanical interlock. Nominal Long-Term Strength (Tal) and Pullout Resistance per Tables S-1 (geotextiles) and S-2 (geogrids). For geotextiles: permeability > reinforced soil permeability; survivability Class 1 per AASHTO M-288. Tal = TULT / (RFCR * RFID * RFD). Construction: subgrade proof-rolled and approved by geotechnical engineer; geosynthetic in continuous longitudinal strips perpendicular to slope; no joints in design strength direction; 100% coverage; track vehicles not allowed on geosynthetic without 6-in (150 mm) soil cover; fill in 12-in (300 mm) max lifts for heavy equipment, 6-in for hand equipment; compaction to 95% AASHTO T-99.

Erosion Control Mat (10.10.2): Pre-qualified materials; Type I: long-term (>2 yr), td > 2 psf to < 5 psf (95-240 Pa); Type II: long-term, td >= 5 psf (240 Pa); staples: U-shaped, 1/8-in wire, min 18-in long for RSS face, 12-in for channels; install within 24 hours of seeding.

Geosynthetic Drainage Composite (10.10.3): 3D polymeric core with geotextile filter. Design based on flow capacity (ASTM D4716), AOS (ASTM D4751), and permeability. Minimum physical properties per Table S3: Class 2 geotextile grab strength 700 N, tear 250 N, puncture 1375 N; Class 3: grab 500 N, tear 180 N. Seams: geotextile flap overlap secured with tape or adhesive; interlocking with upstream edge on top.

Proprietary RSS Systems (10.10.4): Design submittal within 30 days of NTP and 60 days before construction; material submittals 60 days before construction; construction per specification guidelines; measurement per vertical square foot.
key_points: Agency must pre-approve geosynthetic reinforcement, drainage composite, and erosion control materials before project advertisement
RSS fill: 95% AASHTO T-99; max lift 12 in (heavy equipment), 6 in (hand equipment)
Minimum 6 in soil cover before tracked vehicles on geosynthetics
Tractive shear < 2 psf (100 Pa): vegetation + temporary/permanent mat; > 2 psf: permanent mat or armor
Erosion mats installed within 24 hours of seeding; staples min 18-in long for slope face
Geocomposite: core design per ASTM D4716; Class 2 geotextile for standard construction conditions

tables.title: Required Geotextile Reinforcement Properties
tables.content: Ultimate strength TULT per ASTM D4595; Nominal long-term strength Tal = TULT/(RFCR*RFID*RFD); RFCR per ASTM D5262; Classes A and B for different fill types (GW-GM, SW-SM-SC)

tables.title: Required Geogrid Properties
tables.content: Ultimate strength TULT per ASTM D6637; Nominal long-term strength Tal = TULT/(RFCR*RFID*RFD); Classes A and B for different fill types

tables.title: Minimum Physical Property Criteria for Geocomposite Drains in RSS
tables.content: Flow capacity: ASTM D4716 (project specific); AOS: ASTM D4751 (project specific); Permeability: ASTM D4491; Class 2 geotextile: tear 250 N, grab 700 N, puncture 1375 N; Class 3 geotextile: tear 180 N, grab 500 N, puncture 180 N

sections.applicability: RSS construction specifications; geosynthetic reinforcement, drainage, and erosion control
